paragraphs: Children in care in Lincolnshire are looked after by Lincolnshire Fostering Service, run by Lincolnshire County Council, and by the independent agencies listed on this page. The council's service was rated Outstanding by Ofsted in 2023 and describes its training for carers as award-winning and tailored.

The service welcomes single people and couples, whatever their gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, disability or employment, whether or not they are on benefits, rent or own their home, or already have children. You need to be over 21 (there is no upper age limit) and have a spare bedroom. Couples need to have lived together for at least 18 months, and people who smoke or vape cannot foster children under five.

Lincolnshire publishes a weekly allowance for each child, set by the child's age, together with retention bonuses for carers who stay with the service. Our Lincolnshire allowance page sets out the 2026-27 rates.

The council runs “you can foster” information events where you can hear from the team and ask questions. Agencies set their own fees and support, so it is worth speaking to the council and two or three of the agencies below, and asking each about training, out-of-hours help and what they pay, before you choose.
